name: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto
role: President (1971–1973) and prime minister (1973–1977) of Pakistan
summary: Bhutto led Pakistan after the secession of Bangladesh. His government nationalized major industries and banks and redistributed agricultural land. He led the negotiations that produced the 1973 parliamentary constitution and signed the Simla Agreement with India.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Bhutto retained and reorganized the armed forces and appointed their senior leadership.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Bhutto added a federal internal security force to the existing policing institutions and kept it under civilian executive control.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Bhutto's land regulation retained individual holdings below the ceiling and granted private title to cultivating tenants.

ban-interest.rationale: Bhutto's constitution instructed the state to eliminate riba as early as possible in its economic principles.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Under Bhutto's constitution, proposed federal budget grants for ordinary expenditure were put to a vote in the elected National Assembly.

capital-controls.rationale: Bhutto's government maintained foreign exchange controls as an instrument of balance-of-payments policy.

clerical-rule.rationale: Bhutto instituted a parliamentary executive under an elected legislature and gave the Council of Islamic Ideology advisory duties.

collective-farming.rationale: Bhutto distributed resumed farmland by granting it to individual cultivating tenants under paragraph 18 of the 1972 regulation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Bhutto convened the elected National Assembly and used it to frame and adopt the permanent constitution.

direct-action.rationale: Bhutto brought the elected National Assembly into session to frame the constitution and sought a renewed mandate through national elections in 1977.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Bhutto's constitutional settlement had legislators elect the president.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Bhutto urged a free plebiscite on Kashmir's accession in the General Assembly and reaffirmed the obligation to hold it in If I Am Assassinated.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The constitution Bhutto brought into force declared that sovereignty over the universe belongs to Allah and that the people's authority is a delegated trust.

elective-rulers.rationale: Bhutto's constitutional settlement created an elected presidency filled by a vote of legislators.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Bhutto's government placed Karachi, Hyderabad and Lahore under martial law during the April 1977 domestic political crisis.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Bhutto took Pakistan out of SEATO while keeping it a member of the CENTO military pact.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Bhutto's constitution included a chapter of fundamental rights and required supermajorities in the national legislature for constitutional amendments.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The constitutional settlement Bhutto led excluded non-Muslims from the presidency, and his government added a formal religious classification for Ahmadis.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Bhutto inaugurated Pakistan's first nuclear power station in 1972 and his government adopted a program for a series of new civilian generating stations in 1975.

farm-price-support.rationale: Bhutto's government raised administered procurement prices for crops and subsidized seeds, fertilizer, irrigation and agricultural credit.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Bhutto deployed the army against the Baloch insurgency and mobilized backing for the campaign around Pakistan's territorial integrity following Bengali secession.

gradual-change.rationale: Bhutto shifted whole sectors into public ownership in successive large nationalization measures and imposed nationwide land ceilings early in his tenure.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Bhutto's 1976 defense arrangements put effective authority over national security in the hands of the civilian prime minister while the presidency was a separate office.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Bhutto regarded the end of colonial rule as a first step and called for changing the economic relations that left newly independent countries poor.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Bhutto commissioned Pakistan's own nuclear weapons program and assigned national institutions responsibility for carrying it out.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Bhutto's government created the Employees' Old-Age Benefits Institution in 1976 to fund old-age pensions through compulsory social insurance.

land-redistribution.rationale: Bhutto imposed ceilings on large holdings and directed the land above those ceilings to be transferred free of charge to its recorded cultivating tenants.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Article 227 of the constitution Bhutto implemented required laws to conform to the injunctions of Islam in the Quran and Sunnah.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Article 37 of the constitution Bhutto brought into force directed the state to prevent prostitution as a principle of policy.

limit-population.rationale: Bhutto's administration set up a Population Planning Division in 1975 to carry out a new family planning program in response to the high birth rate.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Bhutto's 1976 defense white paper placed the armed forces under civilian control and gave the civilian prime minister the decisive role on national security.

minority-language-support.rationale: Articles 28 and 251 of Bhutto's constitution protected the rights of distinct language communities and explicitly authorized provincial legislation for the teaching, promotion and use of provincial languages.

more-religion-public.rationale: The 1973 constitution made Islam the state religion, provided for Quranic and Islamic instruction, and created institutions for aligning laws with Islam.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Bhutto used the state to run industries and banks and to expand welfare for workers.

no-central-bank.rationale: Bhutto's government retained the State Bank of Pakistan and used it to raise discount rates and tighten credit.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Article 31 of the constitution Bhutto brought into force directed the state to make the teaching of the Quran and Islamiat compulsory for Muslims.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Bhutto brought into force a constitution that protected the preservation and promotion of languages, scripts and cultures and allowed communities to establish institutions for that purpose.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The constitution Bhutto enacted required special attention to disadvantaged classes and provision of necessities to people unable to earn a livelihood.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The constitution Bhutto brought into force vested judicial power in public courts, including the Supreme Court and provincial High Courts.

property-franchise.rationale: Article 51 extended the national franchise on adult citizenship and electoral enrollment with no property qualification.

property-fundamental.rationale: Bhutto's 1972 land regulation transferred acreage over the statutory ceiling to the state without compensating the owners.

public-ownership.rationale: Bhutto took major industrial enterprises into public ownership and extended nationalization to banks and insurance.

racial-franchise.rationale: Bhutto instituted a national adult franchise under a common citizenship qualification across the provinces and ethnic communities.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: In the 1963 General Assembly debate Bhutto condemned apartheid and endorsed equal participation of all ethnic groups in South Africa.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Bhutto's labor legislation imposed profit-sharing and worker participation requirements on covered industrial enterprises and expanded enforcement by labor officials.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Bhutto's government secured the 1974 constitutional amendment that classified both Ahmadi branches as non-Muslim for constitutional and legal purposes.

reserved-seats-excluded-groups.rationale: The parliamentary constitution Bhutto negotiated guaranteed women reserved seats in the National Assembly.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Bhutto proposed international measures to stabilize primary commodity prices and improve developing countries' access to markets for manufactured exports.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Bhutto negotiated mutual withdrawal to either side of the international border after the 1971 war, securing the return of occupied Pakistani territory.

right-to-secede.rationale: Bhutto used federal troops to defeat an armed territorial challenge in Balochistan and justified federal intervention in terms of national integration after Bangladesh's secession.

second-chamber.rationale: The constitution Bhutto brought into force added a Senate with provincial representation alongside the directly elected National Assembly.

separate-church-state.rationale: The constitution Bhutto implemented made Islam the state religion and required institutions to review legislation against Islamic injunctions.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Bhutto increased public investment and established the Ministry of Production to oversee industries taken under state control.

state-harmful.rationale: Bhutto brought forward a constitution that established federal and provincial governments with legislative, fiscal and executive powers.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The constitution Bhutto enacted directed the state to promote Islamic teaching and to enable Muslims to live in accordance with Islamic principles.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: Bhutto's constitution directed the state to help Muslims live according to Islamic principles and to promote Islamic moral standards.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Bhutto retained membership in CENTO, a Cold War military pact with the United Kingdom and ties to US defense policy.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Bhutto dismissed opposition-led provincial administrations and used restrictions on assembly and arrests to contain organized opposition.

unions-good.rationale: Bhutto strengthened trade unions and introduced shop stewards and collective dispute procedures in his 1972 labor policy to protect workers' interests.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Article 44 of the constitution Bhutto instituted capped a president's tenure at two consecutive terms.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Bhutto's land regulation gave tenants individual title to land they cultivated from holdings acquired by the state under the land ceiling.

women-suffrage.rationale: Bhutto's constitutional settlement enfranchised women on the same basis as men and reserved National Assembly seats for women.

workers-councils.rationale: Bhutto negotiated and implemented a constitution vesting legislative authority in a parliament elected on a territorial basis.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Bhutto's 1972 labor policy gave workers representation in industrial management and instituted workplace shop stewards.

notes: Research covered industry and agriculture, labor and welfare, education and religion, constitutional design, civil liberties, electoral competition, foreign relations, energy, population and environmental administration. The foreign-policy review included Bhutto's General Assembly remarks in the UN General Debate Corpus and the contemporaneous US diplomatic record. The environmental review included Pakistan's retrospective reporting on environmental administration and Burki's account of population and energy policy. The 1973 constitution is cited for provisions in force during Bhutto's tenure. Research on methods of change compared the prison manuscript with the parliamentary and electoral record.
